hints.content: The *range* of a function is the set of all the possible function outputs.

According to the graph, the largest number that is an output of $g$ is $9$, and the smallest number is $-4$. Every number between them is also an output of $g$ for some input. Therefore, the range of $g$ is $-4 \leq g(x) \leq 9$.

options.explanation: In most cases outside of this exercise, an image will only show part of the complete graph of a function, so unless we're given further information about the function, we will not be able to tell exactly what the range of the function is.
options.showPrompt: Can we always tell the range of a function from its graph?

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The graph of the function g starts at negative five, zero, which is plotted. Then is increases at a non linear rate to negative two, nine. The function peaks and decreases at a non linear rate to zero, zero. It continues to decrease but at a slower rate until it increases at a non linear rate through the point one, zero. It increases until two, one-half where it decreases at a non linear rate through the point three, zero. It decreases until the point four, negative four, which is plotted. There is a solid vertical line from zero, negative four to zero, nine. Both points are plotted. There is a dotted horizontal line from zero, negative four to four, negative four. There is another dotted horizontal line from zero, nine to negative eight, nine.

hints.content: In conclusion, the range of the function is $-4 \leq g(x) \leq 9$.
